minutes.headline: Library trustees approved amended October minutes; the food forest grant is still undecided on the governor's desk.
minutes.summary: Trustees amended the October minutes, then heard the director's report on the budget, heavy teen room use, and a town-meeting-funded part-time teen librarian. They also heard legal advice on old trust funds, the delayed food forest grant, the director's evaluation timeline, a strategic plan update and a discussion of advocacy. The meeting adjourned by roll call.

votes.motion: Accept the October 15th minutes as amended

budget_items.what_was_said: Salary lines show the vacation buyout with no transfers in. Electricity is on pace, heating is behind, and sewer and water are high on rates and usage.
Director reported library state aid, revolving, gift and trust fund balances. A small LSTA grant fund is negative.
Special town meeting funded the FY27 budget revision that included money for a 19-hour teen room staff librarian.
The designer's contract did not use prevailing wage, which could raise cost in a worst case. Wood chip paths could save some money.
Two proposals came in with a notable price difference.
Sales results reported, not counting electronic payments.

The advocacy plan discussion is deferred to the January agenda.

what_happened.line: Trustees approved the October minutes as amended, the meeting's only recorded vote besides adjournment.
The director reported on the FY27 operating budget and special revenue balances, including one small grant fund running negative.
Trustees heard that a special town meeting funded a part-time teen room staff librarian position in the FY27 budget revision.
On the food forest grant, trustees heard that the designer's contract did not use prevailing wage, which could raise cost in a worst case.
Trustees set a December 6 return date for evaluation materials and deferred the advocacy plan discussion to January.

why_it_matters: The library's FY27 budget lines for heating, water and sewer, and a funded teen room position bear on what the town budget, mostly taxes, spends on library services this year.
A possible prevailing wage cost on the food forest project could change what that grant-funded work ends up costing.
